extracted.intended_audience: Texas Tribune journalists, editors, newsroom staff, contractors, interns, and the public interested in the organization's ethical policies
extracted.subtask_description: A code of ethics setting standards for reporting, sourcing, conflicts of interest, sponsorships, media integrity and use of AI for The Texas Tribune newsroom. It is intended to guide editorial decisions, staff behavior, disclosures and handling of errors and new technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission and nonpartisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune is a nonpartisan, nonprofit media organization whose mission is to provide impartial, informative reporting and an outlet for civic engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism and organizational activities should be driven by this mission; editorial decisions are made by journalists alone and the organization commits to impartial reporting and public-facing civic discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on all platforms must be truthful, transparent and respectful; facts must be accurate, complete and fairly presented; analysis should represent independent judgment, not preferences or those of sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When mistakes occur, correct them quickly, update the story page, and add to the running list of Tribune corrections; do not republish outside content without permission and credit; plagiarism, fabrication and misappropriation of intellectual property are grounds for immediate termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media integrity and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo editors and video producers may improve technical quality but must not alter the substance of media; all photo illustrations, graphics or animations must be clearly labeled as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No alteration of substantive elements of photos, video or audio. If media are manipulated or are illustrative/AI-generated (when applicable), label them clearly so readers are not misled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing and anonymous sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters should try to identify all sources and grant anonymity only when information is critical, the source is reliable and there is no other way to obtain the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not say a person declined comment if they are already quoted anonymously; identify known biases of sources when possible; anonymous sources should be told the reporter will share their identity with a senior editor who will keep it confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-gathering ethics (no deception or payment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not misrepresent themselves or mislead sources to obtain interviews or stories and must always identify themselves as journalists; they do not use hidden cameras or microphones, go undercover or pay for interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple efforts should be made to contact primary subjects and sources of criticism prior to publication; violating these norms undermines credibility and is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must avoid reporting on stories or projects in which they have a vested financial or personal interest and should avoid investments in companies or industries they regularly cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary employment or freelance work must be approved by an editor to prevent conflicts; top editors coordinate with other divisions but editorial independence must be protected; employees with reporting/editing responsibilities must refrain from partisan political activity, including political contributions or displaying partisan signage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor relations transparency and noninterference
rubrics_metrics.description: Donors and sponsors do not receive preferential treatment; contributions are published by year and amount and do not protect donors from investigation or scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that reference or quote a Tribune donor or corporate sponsor who has contributed $1,000 or more will include a written disclosure; fundraisers must inform potential donors that contributions do not entitle them to special treatment or relationships with newsroom staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts, travel and honoraria policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees, contractors and interns involved in reporting or editing will not accept gifts of more than a nominal value from entities that could have an interest in Tribune reporting and must pay their own way for editorial or business travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial employees may accept honoraria only if paid to the Tribune as a tax-deductible donation (not to the journalist); these rules help prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorships and advertising standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune accepts corporate sponsorships, underwriting and permissible advertising that do not compromise editorial integrity; all such support must be clearly and obviously distinguished from editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor or advertiser messages judged false, unlawful or undermining to the Tribune may be removed; corporate support is solicited by business staff and no sponsored content will be produced by Tribune employees; sponsored content must be labeled and visually differentiated to prevent confusion with independent editorial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: TribTalk editorial independence and paid-placement labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion/commentary section TribTalk used columns solicited from thought leaders and was editorially independent from reporters and editors; columns identified as 'paid placement' were visually differentiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors and donors do not determine editorial content; paid placement content must be clearly labeled and visually distinct to avoid confusing readers with independent editorial material.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy — oversight and non-replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune will not use AI to replace journalists and will not publish AI-generated text unless it has gone through a rigorous verification and editing process; generative tools should not be used as primary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must treat AI-generated output as unverified information and use independent verification before publication; the newsroom retains human editorial judgment over any AI-influenced content.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy — disclosure and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must disclose to editors when they used generative tools in the reporting process and must disclose to readers how AI tools were used when they play a role in developing key findings or in journalism products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures should explain how the tools were used and how the newsroom independently confirmed information obtained via AI; transparency applies both internally (to editors) and externally (to audiences).

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy — permitted uses and cautious experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribune journalists may experiment with AI for tasks such as data analysis, transcription, headline/SEO and social platform writing, but must be critical of the tools and treat outputs as unverified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of AI for these production tasks is allowed but requires independent verification of any substantive claims derived from AI; experimentation is encouraged but supervised.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy — confidentiality and data security
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must avoid putting confidential information such as anonymous source names or privately obtained documents into third-party AI tools and should discuss new AI tools with managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before using a new AI tool, staff should disclose usage to managers and assess security and accuracy risks; sensitive information must not be exposed to external AI services.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy — images, media and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune will not use AI to generate images for news stories and does not alter elements of photos, video or audio; if AI-generated images are the newsworthy subject of a story, they will be clearly labeled with a watermark and caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No AI-manipulated images are published as news photography; if discussed as the subject of reporting, AI images must be clearly identified to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy — control over use of Tribune journalism as model training data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune may selectively block some AI technologies from scraping the Tribune website to add training data for their models and will review such tools case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The newsroom will evaluate benefits and drawbacks of preventing third-party agents from using Tribune content for model training and make decisions based on editorial and organizational interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy — non-editorial staff AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff on marketing, communications, product, revenue, operations and other non-editorial teams are encouraged to experiment with AI for non-journalistic tasks, subject to manager disclosure and attention to security and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-editorial experimentation is permitted but must be coordinated with managers and assessed for risks; editorial restrictions (e.g., no confidential data in third-party tools) still apply where relevant.
